findings.title: GC claim holds one synchronous writer transaction across every deferred/pinned page
findings.cause: LIMIT 128 bounds each retired SELECT, but while(true) stays inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE callback until an eligible row or complete exhaustion. Every skipped row is hydrated. run deadline checked only before claim; admission cancellation does not interrupt started transaction. Offline import preserves arbitrary resource counts independently of runtime caps.
findings.impact: A valid deferred/imported or durable-pinned ledger blocks the event loop and all competing SQL writers despite maxDeletesPerRun=1/runTimeoutMs=5. Actual 25ms writer rejected on 4096/16384-row arms; one-row negative controls committed. No default-budget failure or Linux/Windows timing was measured.
findings.correction: Bound rows/work per claim transaction and yield/release between batches. Preserve exact pin/lease/claim predicates, re-read authority at destructive claim, and use explicit progress state so repeated sweeps do not permanently rescan only oldest blocked entries. Preserve intended candidate ordering or document/approve any changed ordering. Add future-backoff, NULL/exact durable pin, all-leased, late eligible and concurrent-writer controls.

findings.status: causal source path plus isolated phase measurement
findings.title: GC deferred accounting hydrates the whole backlog in one synchronous read snapshot after the claim budget
findings.cause: SELECT all retired/deleting keys followed by readResource and pin lookup for each row; no paging/yield/deadline applies. Even zero-deferred all-pinned rows take this path.
findings.impact: Measured phase/timer delay 263.2ms for 4096 all-pinned rows with deferred=0; 625.9ms for 16384 future rows. Claim-only lock timing is separately recorded; total minus claim is not claimed as an exact isolated count-only duration.
findings.correction: Avoid full JS resource hydration for count/accounting and establish a bounded responsiveness strategy while preserving deferred/pin semantics. An aggregate/filter SQL projection may reduce hydration, but do not claim a wall-time bound merely from a single SQL statement. Add an explicit large zero-deferred pinned control and event-loop responsiveness control.

findings.status: confirmed static regression; cross-packet P4 caller, previously recorded bounded review finding
findings.title: SQL cache clear retains memory caches on durable clear failure and conflicts with approved #1244 reset policy
findings.cause: SQL branch invokes synchronous clearSharedSessions before clearing memory; catch returns silently. Memory clearing is deferred to a successful COMMIT. The current main JSON behavior clears memory before best-effort durable work; approved #1244 requires immediate memory reset and awaited best-effort cleanup.
findings.impact: The clear call can complete while the old degraded-store fallback cache survives. Added tests explicitly preserve old cached ID on failed/uncertain COMMIT, so green tests do not establish the authorized reset behavior.
findings.correction: Coordinate with P4/#1244: preserve immediate reset at the public clear entry point and approved Promise completion/best-effort policy; retain COMMIT hooks for ordinary publication/eviction effects. Do not apply ordinary publication rollback semantics to the independent reset command. Add failed durable cleanup with immediate empty fallback-cache negative control.
